newsitem.title: FRANCE: France gives retiring Christopher French novels.
newsitem.headline: France gives retiring Christopher French novels.

text.p: France took gentle revenge on Wednesday for decades of invasion from America by Mickey Mouse and hamburgers by presenting retiring U.S. Secretary of State Warren Christopher with five French novels -- in French.
Foreign Minister Herve de Charette handed over the books, all of which have won literary prizes in France this year, at a joint news conference with Christopher who is on a 48-hour visit to Paris.
They were tied up in a ribbon of the French national colours -- red, white and blue.

De Charette said he was presenting the "petit cadeau" (little gift) to Christopher "because I think he will have plenty of time for reading" following his retirement next January after four years at the helm of the State Department.
He said the gift would also help Christopher deepen his knowledge of the French language -- "which is already greater than you think", he added generously.
"Thank you very much, Mr Minister, I will look forward to taking these to California with me, and they'll be good companions," Christopher responded. "They will remind me of our good times together."

The best known of the French prizes is the Prix Goncourt, won only on Tuesday by Pascale Roze for her first novel, "Le Chasseur Zero" (Fighter Plane Zero), about a woman who investigates the death of her father at the hands of a Japanese kamikaze pilot.
De Charette said he was making the gift to prove that journalists who asserted that Franco-American relations were in bad shape were "completely mistaken".
